title: Stacked evals scratchpad — Nora Chen
content:
High-level idea:

This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight, composable "stacked" evaluation approach: compose very small, cheap probes (unit checks) + medium-weight scenario tests + a small corpus of heavy human-reviewed regression cases. The goal: get fast signal on degradations after quantization, kernel swaps, or rollout to Dedicated pools, without running the full eval suite every PR.

Motivation / problem statements:
- Full eval runs are expensive and slow; false negatives (missed regressions) happen in production.
- Teams want a quick gate for model-serving changes (quantization bits, batching policy tweaks, fallback policies) that catches the majority of common regressions within minutes/hours.
- Need to balance cost, signal-to-noise, and developer UX (fast but actionable).

Design sketch (stack layers):
1) Unit probes (10s–100s examples) — deterministic checks for tokenization, special-token handling, simple instruction-following. Run on every CI commit.
   - Examples: stop-sequence adherence, exact-answer for short fact Qs, consistent function-call output shape.
   - Lightweight, no human review.
2) Scenario minibatches (hundreds of examples) — representative synthetic + sampled real examples per workload (chat, summarization, rerank). Run nightly or on pre-release builds.
   - Includes prefix-cache-reuse cases, long-context stitching, and typical customer prompts from Hosted API logs (sampled and anonymized).
3) Regression trove (50–200 curated cases) — human-labeled golden outputs, edge cases discovered in incident postmortems. Run weekly and before major rollouts.
   - Prioritized per-product risk: billing-sensitive paths get stricter checks.

Signal plumbing / metrics to report:
- Delta metrics vs baseline (absolute and normalized): token-level perplexity not useful alone — prefer task-specific accuracy/utility and "+/- quality" signals.
- Percent-change alarm thresholds (e.g., >6% failure in unit probes or >2x latency p95 only for Client Tier A).
- Composite "health score" that weights layers: unit probes 40%, scenario minibatches 35%, regression trove 25%.

Operational constraints / implementation notes:
- Minibatches should be cheap: use cached KV responses where possible and replay model variants with identical prompts.
- For Dedicated/private customers, run localized copies; allow smaller trove but preserve signal parity.
- Prefer deterministic seeding and pinned model versions for reproducibility.
- Use streaming outputs to flag early-mode hallucinations (e.g., improbable token next-token probability below threshold).

Quick literature & reading takeaways (notes):
- Small probes conceptually similar to "unit tests for models" (blog posts from 2029–2031 argue for short, focused checks). Key point: they catch syntactic/regression faults fast but not semantic drift.
- NeurIPS 2031 workshop paper (applied evals) argued for layered evals and synthetic scenario generation; relevant techniques for constructing scenario minibatches.
- Recent arXiv on lightweight evaluation scheduling suggests fractal sampling: more frequent small tests + probabilistic sampling of heavy tests. Matches our stacked idea.

Immediate experiments to run (priority order):
1) Create 50 unit probes for Hosted API baseline model (verify tokenization, stop sequences, function call consistency). Target: 3m run time.
2) Build 200-sample scenario minibatch for "summarize-legal" workload by sampling anonymized logs and a few synthetic hard prompts. Run nightly for two weeks and measure stability.
3) Curate a 30-case regression trove from last 6 months' incidents (SRE + CS), add golden outputs and run weekly.

Evaluation dashboard idea (minimal):
- Single-pane health with layer breakdown + trend sparkline (7d, 30d).
- Click-through from any failing probe to: prompt, model version(s), recent commits (linked PR/CI), and last time it failed.
- Annotate whether failure is "semantic" vs "formatting/IO" so ops can triage.

Open questions / forks to consider:
- How to avoid leakage from customer logs when sampling scenario minibatches? (anonymize, synthetically augment)
- Cost allocation: should Hosted API users implicitly subsidize frequent nightly runs? Or charge as an Eval add-on?
- How to pick thresholds automatically (adaptive thresholds) vs static? Consider historical baseline + MAD-based thresholds.

Notes for Redwood Optimize integration:
- Tie stacked-eval health score into rollout policies: fail fast on large degradation in unit probes, allow canary if minibatches show marginal regression but trove is clean.
- Suggest automated rollback if trove fails on critical security/privacy-related prompts.

Short-term deliverables (two-week sprint):
- M1: Implement 50 unit probes + CI runner (owner: Nora) — due 2032-01-10
- M2: Prototype scenario minibatch generator and nightly runner (owner: Evan) — due 2032-01-17
- M3: Hook probe failures into a minimal dashboard (owner: Hannah) — due 2032-01-21

Random ideas / seeds to revisit later:
- Use a small ensemble of cheaper quantized variants to fuzz-test for nondeterministic regressions (if variants disagree beyond threshold, flag).
- Lightweight human-in-the-loop sampling: when minibatch shows drift, surface 10 examples to an on-call reviewer for quick accept/reject.

End of scratchpad for now. Will iterate as experiments produce data.
